subject: geography
title: KS3 Geography — Geographical Skills Reading
subtitle: Passage pack for map skills, relief and fieldwork interpretation
description: These short reading passages help students explain and apply key geographical skills in context. The questions mix retrieval, inference and explanation so the pack can support both revision and exam-style practice.

data.sourcePassage: Map scale allows geographers to turn a short map measurement into a real distance on the ground. On a 1:50,000 map, 1 centimetre represents 500 metres, so 2 centimetres equals 1 kilometre. A 1:25,000 map shows a smaller area but gives more detail, which is useful for footpaths and field boundaries. Straight-line distance can be measured with a ruler, but curved features such as rivers and winding roads are better measured with string or a flexible edge. Students often lose marks when they forget to convert metres into kilometres or when they use the wrong scale for the map they are given.

questions.question: On a 1:50,000 map, how much real distance does 1 centimetre represent?
Why might a geographer prefer a 1:25,000 map to a 1:50,000 map for walking fieldwork?
questions.modelAnswer: A 1:25,000 map gives more detail, so it is better for features such as footpaths, walls and field boundaries.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is the best way to measure a winding river, and why?
questions.modelAnswer: Use string or a flexible edge because a curved feature cannot be measured accurately with a straight ruler alone.

questions.question: Explain why converting units correctly matters when using scale in an exam.
questions.modelAnswer: If students do not convert metres into kilometres correctly, they can reach the wrong final answer even if their measuring method was sensible.

data.sourcePassage: Grid references and bearings help geographers describe location precisely. A four-figure grid reference identifies a whole square by reading eastings first and northings second. A six-figure reference is more accurate because it adds tenths across and tenths up within that square. Bearings add another layer of precision because they show direction using degrees measured clockwise from north. For example, east is 090° and south is 180°. Common mistakes include reading northings first, measuring anti-clockwise or forgetting to write bearings with three digits.

questions.question: Which part of a grid reference is read first?
Why is a six-figure grid reference more accurate than a four-figure grid reference?
questions.modelAnswer: It gives tenths across and tenths up within the square, so it pinpoints a more exact position.

questions.question: What is the bearing for a place directly east?
Explain how two different mistakes could make a bearing answer unreliable.
questions.modelAnswer: If a student measures anti-clockwise or starts from the wrong line, the direction is wrong. If they forget three digits, the answer is not written in the standard map-skills form.

data.sourcePassage: Relief is the shape and height of the land, and contour lines are one of the main ways maps show it. Each contour line joins places of equal height. Close contour lines show a steep slope because the height changes quickly over a short distance, while wide contour lines show a gentle slope. Circular contours often show a hill, and V-shaped contours often suggest a valley with a river flowing through it. Spot heights give the exact height of one point. Away from local map reading, geographers also use latitude and longitude to locate places on Earth. Latitude measures north or south of the Equator, while longitude measures east or west of the Prime Meridian at Greenwich.

questions.question: What do contour lines join together?
questions.modelAnswer: Contour lines join places of equal height.

questions.question: What can you infer about a slope if the contour lines are far apart?
questions.modelAnswer: The slope is likely to be gentle because the height changes slowly over a longer distance.

questions.question: How do spot heights improve the information given by contour lines?
questions.modelAnswer: They provide the exact height at one point, while contour lines mainly show patterns of equal height and slope shape.

questions.question: Explain why latitude and longitude are useful beyond ordinary map reading.
questions.modelAnswer: They allow places to be located globally and are useful for navigation, GPS, climate zones and air travel.

data.sourcePassage: A simple traffic survey can help students investigate whether traffic volume increases closer to a town centre. In the case study, students chose three locations, counted traffic for ten minutes and recorded different vehicle types using a tally chart. The totals were 37 vehicles on a residential street, 99 on the main road and 159 in the town centre. This supported the hypothesis that traffic volume would be higher near the centre. The investigation was easy to repeat and produced quantitative data, but it also had limits. Only one time of day was used, weather may have affected the results and the sample size was small. Repeating the survey at different times and on different days would make the enquiry fairer and more reliable.

questions.question: Which location had the highest traffic count?
questions.modelAnswer: The town centre had the highest traffic count.

questions.question: What evidence in the passage supports the hypothesis?
questions.modelAnswer: Traffic totals increased from 37 on the residential street to 99 on the main road and 159 in the town centre, so the busiest place was closest to the centre.

questions.question: Why might using only one time of day weaken the investigation?
questions.modelAnswer: Traffic levels change during the day, so one time period may not represent normal patterns and could make the results less reliable.

questions.question: Explain one improvement that would make the survey fairer or more reliable.
questions.modelAnswer: Repeating the count at different times or on different days would reduce the effect of unusual traffic conditions and give a more dependable pattern.
